description: AI-assisted demonstration mapping proposals; NOT legal advice, an applicability determination, control equivalence, or evidence of implementation/compliance.
direction: source (EU AI Act) -> target (NIST AI RMF GenAI Profile)

source_catalog.title: EU Artificial Intelligence Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — OSCAL Catalog

target_catalog.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework Generattive AI Profile

seed_conversion_note: Resolve exact tenant-scoped catalog and revision UUIDs after catalog import, then convert entries through the existing MappingService. OSCAL mapping collection import does not yet exist.

mappings.target_control_title: Establish policies restricting the use of GAI to create child sexual abuse materials (CSAM) or other nonconsensual intimate imagery.
mappings.justification: Both address non-consensual intimate imagery. The AI RMF action recommends restricting GAI use through policy; the EU control states a prohibition subject to precise conditions. A policy alone does not establish compliance.

mappings.source_control_title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
mappings.target_control_title: Consider the following, or similar, factors when updating or defining risk tiers for GAI: Abuses and risks to information integrity; Cadence of vendor releases and updates; Data protection requirements; Dependencies between GAI and other IT or data systems; Harm in physical environments; Human review of GAI system outputs; Legal or regulatory requirements; Presentation of obscene, objectionable, toxic, invalid or untruthful output; Psychological impacts to humans (e.g., anthropomorphization, algorithmic aversion, emotional entanglement); Immediate and long term impacts; Internal vs. external use; Unreliable decision making capabilities, validity, adaptability, and variability of GAI system performance over time.
mappings.justification: Both concern risk classification informed by context and legal requirements. AI RMF risk tiers do not determine the legal high-risk classification under Article 6.

mappings.target_control_title: Establish policies, procedures, and processes detailing risk measurement in context of use with standardized measurement protocols and structured public feedback exercises such as AI red-teaming or independent external audits.
mappings.justification: Both involve risk-measurement processes and ongoing governance. The AI RMF action covers assessment practices, not the entire legally prescribed lifecycle risk management system.

mappings.target_control_title: Document training data sources to trace the origin and provenance of AI-generated content.
mappings.justification: Both refer to documenting data sources and provenance. The AI RMF action covers only one aspect of the broader Article 10 data quality, governance and bias requirements.

mappings.target_control_title: Implement version control for models and datasets to track changes and facilitate rollback if necessary.
mappings.justification: Version control of models and datasets can support keeping technical documentation current and traceable. It does not cover all Annex IV documentation requirements.

mappings.target_control_title: Deploy logging and monitoring tools to continuously track AI system performance and flag abnormal behavior.
mappings.justification: Both address AI-system logging and monitoring. The AI RMF action is broader operational monitoring and does not specify the legally required events and retention context.

mappings.target_control_title: Document system requirements, ownership, and AI actor roles and responsibilities for human oversight of GAI systems.
mappings.justification: Both involve human oversight and documented responsibilities. Documenting roles alone does not provide the operational intervention and control capabilities required by Article 14.

mappings.target_control_title: Perform AI red-teaming to assess resilience against malicious behavior, including malicious code generation, prompt injection, adversarial examples, data poisoning, and model extraction.
mappings.justification: Adversarial testing can help evaluate cybersecurity and robustness. Red-teaming addresses only part of Article 15, which also covers accuracy and ongoing resilience.

mappings.target_control_title: Connect new GAI policies, procedures, and processes to existing model, data, and IT governance and to legal, compliance, and risk functions.
mappings.justification: Both call for integrating AI policies and procedures into organizational governance. The EU quality management system mandates substantially more specific processes and evidence.

mappings.source_control_title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems
mappings.target_control_title: Conduct impact assessments on how AI-generated content might affect different social, economic, and cultural groups.
mappings.justification: Both involve analyzing potential impacts on people and groups. The AI RMF action does not replace a role- and use-case-specific fundamental-rights impact assessment.

mappings.source_control_title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
mappings.target_control_title: Disclose use of GAI to end users.
mappings.justification: Both concern disclosing AI use to end users. Article 50 includes specific system categories, presentation, timing and accessibility requirements not captured by the AI RMF action.

mappings.target_control_title: Develop and update GAI system incident response and recovery plans and procedures to address the following: Review and maintenance of policies and procedures to account for newly encountered uses; Review and maintenance of policies and procedures for detection of unanticipated uses; Verify response and recovery plans account for the GAI system supply chain; Verify response and recovery plans are updated for and include necessary details to communicate with downstream GAI system actors.
mappings.justification: Both involve incident response and downstream communication. An incident-response plan is not equivalent to the Article 73 duty to report qualifying incidents to the competent authorities within deadlines.
